content: Plant your own garden and decorate your own soul, instead of waiting for someone to bring you flowers.
author: Jorge Luis Borges
sourceWork: Jorge Luis Borges's Essays & Philosophical Writings
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. Thinking about doing something gives us a comfortable dopamine hit of progress without any of the actual friction. We often use over-researching and planning as socially acceptable disguises for fear of starting.

In Jorge Luis Borges's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Clarity follows action; it does not precede it. You cannot think your way into a new way of living—you have to act your way into a new way of understanding. The smallest real-world step beats the most brilliant theory.
reflectionPrompt: Where in your current routine are you choosing convenient illusion over uncomfortable truth?
